security_audit.summary: The skill is intended for read-only Linear milestone lookup, but it requires a Linear API key and references a workspace environment file. Most shell-execution detections are Markdown formatting false positives, while the Bun command examples and secret handling remain real trust concerns.

remediation.suggestion: Document the minimum required Linear token scope and recommend a dedicated token only for this skill.
Avoid relying on a workspace .env file, or clearly require it to be ignored by version control.

remediation.issue: Implementation code is not included in the audited package
remediation.suggestion: Publish the script that reads milestones with the skill, so reviewers can inspect API and filesystem behavior.
Explain the trust boundary for running the Bun command and keep arguments structured without shell interpolation.

finding_verdicts.reason: The manifest declares LINEAR_API_KEY as required setup, so the skill needs access to a sensitive Linear credential. A community skill with this token can read private Linear project data if misused.
Line 11 uses Markdown code spans around LINEAR_API_KEY and .env text. There is no shell backtick execution or command substitution on this line.
Line 16 documents an environment variable and .env path inside Markdown code spans. It does not execute a shell command.
The fenced bash block shows a Bun command that runs a local skill script. This is intentional CLI behavior, but it still requires trusting local executable code from the community package.
The detected text is the closing Markdown fence and the start of an options list. It is documentation formatting, not executable Ruby or shell backtick usage.
Line 27 documents the --project option in a Markdown code span. It does not invoke a command or interpolate user input into a shell.
Line 28 documents the --all option in a Markdown code span. No command execution occurs on this line.
Line 29 documents the --limit option in Markdown. It is not shell backtick execution.
Line 30 documents the --json option in a Markdown code span. There is no executable command on this line.

The examples show Bun commands that execute the local milestone script with user-provided project arguments. The commands are documented and expected, but they create a real local execution trust boundary.
The finding starts at the closing Markdown fence and continues into output guidance. It does not contain an executable shell construct.
Line 46 mentions --json and jq in Markdown code spans as output guidance. It does not execute jq or any shell command.
The hardcoded URL is a public documentation link to bun.sh for runtime installation. It is not a network call from the skill or a data exfiltration endpoint.
Line 11 tells users the API key may be stored in <git-root>/.env. That hidden environment file can contain sensitive credentials and must be handled as a secret source.
Line 16 repeats that LINEAR_API_KEY may come from <git-root>/.env. The hidden file reference is intentional, but it is still sensitive filesystem access.
Line 11 requires LINEAR_API_KEY for the skill to operate. That credential grants access to Linear data and is a real secret-handling risk.
Line 16 documents LINEAR_API_KEY in the environment or .env file. This confirms the skill depends on a sensitive API credential.
Line 11 instructs use of a git-root .env file for the Linear API key. Environment files often hold multiple secrets, so a community skill that depends on them requires careful trust review.
Line 16 explicitly pairs LINEAR_API_KEY with <git-root>/.env. This is sensitive environment-file access, even though it is described as configuration.

content.user_title: Read Linear Milestones from the CLI
content.value_statement: Teams need quick visibility into Linear milestones without opening the web app. This skill runs a read-only CLI workflow for filtered milestone lists.
actual_capabilities: Lists Linear project milestones from a command-line workflow.
Filters milestone results by project name.
Lists milestones across all projects with the --all option.
Limits result count with the --limit option.
Outputs milestone data as JSON when requested.
Uses LINEAR_API_KEY for authenticated Linear access.
limitations: Requires Bun to be installed before use.
Requires a valid LINEAR_API_KEY in the environment or .env file.
Does not create, update, or delete Linear milestones.
Implementation code is not included in the audited skill package.

output_examples.output: The terminal shows a milestone table for matching Linear project results.

output_examples.output: The terminal displays a concise cross-project milestone list capped at 10 results.

output_examples.input: Return milestones for Monticello in JSON format.
output_examples.output: The terminal displays structured milestone data suitable for another reporting tool.

best_practices: Use a dedicated Linear API key with the smallest available permissions.
Confirm Bun and the skill script are installed before requesting milestone data.
Use project filters when you only need one project to reduce output noise.
anti_patterns: Do not commit LINEAR_API_KEY or .env files to source control.
Do not use this skill for milestone changes because it is read-only.
Do not ask for broad all-project output when a project filter is enough.

faq.question: Does this skill modify Linear milestones?
faq.answer: No. The documented commands are read-only and list milestone information.

faq.question: What credential does it need?
faq.answer: It needs LINEAR_API_KEY in the environment or an approved .env file.

faq.question: Can it filter by project?
faq.answer: Yes. Use a project name filter, and partial matching is documented.

faq.question: Can it show milestones for all projects?
faq.answer: Yes. The --all option lists milestones across projects.

faq.question: Can it produce machine-readable output?
faq.answer: Yes. The --json option returns structured output for tools that can consume it.

faq.question: What should I review before installing it?
faq.answer: Review the script implementation and API key handling because the package uses sensitive Linear credentials.
